messages:
ana: FYI I'm seeing the SDK lose generic information when consumed from a Cloudflare edge worker bundle. Types become `any` downstream even though node tsc shows correct types. Anyone tried consuming the SDK from edge bundles?

ryan: yep. Common culprits: 1) bundler inlines or rewrites runtime exports so .d.ts no longer maps to the code path, 2) package `exports` may not advertise a types-only ESM entry, 3) dts generation that emits CJS-style `export =` can cause widening.

ana: (typo: ana) I use `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` and then `const client = new Redwood<MySchema>()`. Methods like `client.generate` show parameter types as `any`.

sam: can you paste package.json from node_modules/@redwood/inference and the top of the emitted dist .d.ts?

ana: package.json has: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } }

The d.ts top lines show `export = RedwoodClient;` and a generated `declare function request(...args: any[]): Promise<any>;`

ryan: there it is. `export =` + non-generic method signatures. The published d.ts lost method generics. SDK build probably flattens generated types making methods `any`.

irene: short-term for consumers: 1) patch-package the package to swap in a hand-edited d.ts with correct generic method signatures, 2) mark the SDK external in your edge bundle so the runtime code isn't bundled (keeps tsc happy), 3) import types directly from a types-only path if SDK publishes one (e.g., `@redwood/inference/types`).

ana: externalizing works but increases edge's cold start (we're trying to avoid network fetch). Patch-package is messy across CI. Any other suggestions?

sam: ask SDK to publish a pure ESM types entrypoint and avoid `export =`. Also request they add a tiny compile test: an ESM project that consumes the package and asserts `tsc --noEmit` keeps generic inference. We should file a repo issue with repro.

typebot: Created issue #4537: "DX: published d.ts have non-generic method signatures causing any widening for ESM/edge consumers" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4537 :robot_face:

ryan: also check `tsconfig.json` in the edge project. Setting `moduleResolution` to `bundler` can help modern ESM-only packages. `importsNotUsedAsValues: 'preserve'` sometimes prevents bundler transformations from removing type-only imports.

ana: tried `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and `importsNotUsedAsValues: 'preserve'` — no luck; still `any` after esbuild bundle. Local `tsc` is fine. So it's definitely bundle-time.

irene: one more trick: add a local ambient augmentation that narrows the SDK method signatures in your repo until upstream fixes it. Example:
```ts
declare module '@redwood/inference' {
  interface RedwoodClient<T = any> {
    request<TIn>(opts: { input: TIn; }): Promise<Response<TIn>>;
  }
}
```
This buys time for a few teams.

ana: I will do an augmentation as a temporary workaround and add a CI step that runs a tiny compile after bundling. Filing an internal infra task to make SDK external for now.

sam: I'll coordinate with SDK team on the issue. We should ask them to stop emitting `export =` in the public dts and to run a minimal edge/ESM TS compile in release CI. Also request they bump minor and cut a patch release.

ryan: long term: SDK should publish `exports` like "./": { "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/esm/index.js" } where the types path matches the import path exactly. That avoids resolution fallbacks to CJS dts.

ana: thanks everyone. I have the augmentation and patch-package plan as fallbacks, plus the issue link. Will update when infra externalizes the SDK. :thumbsup:
